clue.text: Invalid transport that's occupied by professor in South-West

parts.note: Bath is a spa city in the south-west of England
a professor holds a chair, the post being named for the seat

explanation.surface: A wheelchair-like vehicle in which some West Country academic sits.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is an English spa city famous for the elderly visitors once wheeled about in these chairs.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old hooded wheeled seat for carrying a sick or disabled person, an invalid's conveyance.

clue.text: Breakfast food successfully brought home

definitions.meaning: cured pork rashers eaten at breakfast
the idiom of bringing home the ... means earning a living or succeeding

explanation.surface: Someone cooks the morning fry-up after a triumphant return.
explanation.definitionFit: Cured pork is a breakfast staple, and the idiom names what a successful breadwinner brings home.

clue.text: American singer taking time, lots of it? Right

parts.note: a long time is an age, so lots of time is 'an age'

explanation.surface: A US vocalist who takes ages over a performance, apparently correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' here is a songbird, not a vocalist: this is a brightly coloured American bird.
explanation.definitionFit: These are colourful songbirds of the Americas, so a bird singer from America.

clue.text: Attempt to win in certain areas of sport with it

parts.note: tennis, squash and other games are played on courts
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A trendy bid for victory on the tennis or squash courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooing is the attempt to win someone's affections, a romantic pursuit.

clue.text: Achieved success with rice cooked for so long abroad

parts.note: someone who has arrived has achieved success

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of the word rice are worked into a new mixture

explanation.surface: A chef triumphs with a rice dish, then says goodbye in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns RICE into ERCI.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Italian farewell, a foreign way to say goodbye or so long.

clue.text: Gun for serviceman?

definitions.meaning: to gun an engine is to ... it hard
a reverend, short form ..., is a man who conducts church services

explanation.surface: A weapon issued to a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun' is a verb about engines and 'serviceman' a clergyman taking services, not a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To gun a motor is to race it, and the clergyman's short title fits a man leading services.

clue.text: Class outside university found place for debate

indicators.note: outside says the class word goes round the university letter

parts.note: a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A class meeting outside the university has found somewhere to argue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a meeting place or medium for public discussion, as in ancient Rome.

clue.text: Short movie about American musket

indicators.note: about says the shortened word goes round the American letters
short asks for the movie word to lose its final letter

parts.note: a film is a movie

explanation.surface: A brief film about an American firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short movie' reads as a short film, but 'Short' only clips the last letter; 'about' then wraps FIL round the American letters. Fusiliers took their name from this weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusil was a light flintlock musket, the old firearm carried by fusiliers.

clue.text: Ship remembered in verse as example, at no stage given up

indicators.note: in a down clue, given up means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: EG is short for 'for example'
at no stage means never

explanation.surface: A ship commemorated in poetry, set as an example of never surrendering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given up' sounds like surrender, but in a down clue it turns EGNEVER upwards. Tennyson's ballad 'The Revenge' tells of Sir Richard Grenville's ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Revenge was Grenville's Elizabethan warship, celebrated in Tennyson's ballad of that name.

clue.text: Teacher with set of answers needed for Common Entrance?

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher
a key is the set of answers to a test

explanation.surface: A teacher holding the answer sheet for the Common Entrance exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Common Entrance is the British exam for entry to private secondary schools; here it is read as a door shared by many.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass key opens many locks, so it is needed for a doorway in common use.

clue.text: Best to follow William's example

definitions.meaning: to best someone is to defeat them
William the Conqueror invaded England in 1066

explanation.surface: Being the finest by imitating a man called William.
explanation.definitionFit: To best an opponent is to beat them, which is also what William the Conqueror did to England.

clue.text: Regarding incomplete duplication of travel document

indicators.note: incomplete says the doubled run loses its last letter
duplication says the travel document is written twice

parts.note: a visa is an entry permit stamped in a passport

explanation.surface: A query about a partly copied passport stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duplication of' gives VISAVISA and 'incomplete' drops the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase is used to mean in relation to, or concerning, something.

clue.text: Late activity near West End

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: end asks for the last letter of the word West

explanation.surface: A late-night event close to London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatreland; here 'West End' is just the last letter of 'West'.
explanation.definitionFit: A night out, a quiz night or opening night is an evening event, activity held late.

clue.text: Policeman unofficially leaving it out of order

indicators.note: out of order says the letters are jumbled into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A rogue officer leaves something out of turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-appointed enforcer of law acts as a police officer without any authority.

clue.text: Girl entering island group with inferior craftsman

indicators.note: entering says the girl goes into the island group

parts.note: GB, Great Britain, is a group of islands
a lass is a girl
lower means inferior in rank or quality

explanation.surface: A young woman arrives at some islands with a second-rate artisan.
explanation.walkthrough: GB stands for Great Britain, read here as a group of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass-blower is an artisan shaping molten glass, a skilled craft trade.

clue.text: That woman's energy goes in a short time

indicators.note: goes in says the energy letter is put inside the time abbreviation

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour, a time written short
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A woman's vigour flags after a brief interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a short time' looks like a brief period, but it is an abbreviated time unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun for a female means belonging to that woman.

clue.text: Combining ingredient for beer with spirit is child's play

parts.note: hops flavour beer
Scotch is whisky, a spirit

explanation.surface: Mixing beer and whisky is easy, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child's play' is literal: a children's game, not something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a playground game of hopping across chalked squares, literally a child's play.

clue.text: One looks for others to play this game

definitions.text: One looks for others to play this game

parts.words: One looks for others to play this game
parts.note: describes a children's game where one player seeks the others who have concealed themselves

explanation.surface: Someone looking around for playmates.
explanation.definitionFit: In this children's game one seeker hunts for the other players, who conceal themselves.

clue.text: Labour endlessly keeping people in office thus?

definitions.text: Labour endlessly keeping people in office thus?

parts.words: Labour endlessly keeping people in office thus?
parts.note: read as office workers chained to their work stations, endlessly labouring, rather than a party in power

explanation.surface: A political party clinging to government for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' and 'office' suggest the British political party in power; the clue means workers tied to their work tables.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stuck at a work table in an office is tied to sedentary work all day.

clue.text: Different expressions Sara, perhaps, varied

indicators.note: varied says the letters are changed round into another order

explanation.surface: A woman called Sara might change how she puts things.
explanation.definitionFit: Restatements of a text in other words are alternative expressions of the same meaning.

clue.text: People must be disturbed to read it

definitions.text: People must be disturbed to read it

parts.words: People must be disturbed to read it
parts.note: describes a statute formally read out to disperse an unruly crowd

explanation.surface: A text only the mentally troubled can make sense of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' suggests mental illness; it means a rowdy crowd, to which the old Riot Act was read in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riot Act was read aloud to unruly crowds of twelve or more before they could be dispersed.

clue.text: Judge, by way of example

definitions.meaning: used to introduce an instance, like 'for instance'

explanation.surface: A judge giving an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate something is to judge it, and the word also introduces an instance, like 'for example'.

clue.text: Work on paper with base inside outfit

indicators.note: inside says the base word goes within the outfit word

parts.note: a suit is an outfit of clothes
a bed is a base, as a bed of concrete

explanation.surface: Doing a job on a newspaper with a foundation layer in a costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work on paper' means editing for a newspaper, not drawing or writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct copy for publication is a newspaper editor's work on the paper.

clue.text: Bad-tempered old battle-axe gets the bird

parts.note: cross means angry or bad-tempered
a bill was a medieval halberd-like weapon

explanation.surface: A grumpy old woman is booed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battle-axe' suggests a fierce woman and 'gets the bird' a booing; both are literal here.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a finch with crossed mandible tips for prising seeds from cones.

clue.text: Hard for those who are barefoot and penniless

definitions.text: Hard for those who are barefoot
definitions.meaning: rocky ground is hard on bare feet

explanation.surface: Rough going for poor folk without shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky ground is hard underfoot, and 'stony broke' is British slang for penniless.

clue.text: Opus on BBC, half-hearted kind of jazz

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after
half-hearted asks for one of the two middle letters to go

parts.note: the Beeb is a nickname for the BBC, the British broadcaster
op is the abbreviation for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A musical work broadcast on the BBC, played without much enthusiasm, in a jazz style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of BEEB's two middle Es, giving BEB.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the fast, complex jazz style of 1940s players like Charlie Parker.

clue.text: Keeper of diary gets excited about year

indicators.note: about says the excited word goes round the year letter

parts.note: peps, as in peps up, becomes lively

explanation.surface: A diarist grows animated about the passing year.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys kept a famous diary of 1660s London.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys is the famous seventeenth-century English diarist, keeper of a celebrated journal.

clue.text: London accepts New Age dress

indicators.note: accepts says London's word takes the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: town, to Londoners, means London

indicators.note: new means the letters of Age are remade in another order

explanation.surface: The capital embraces New Age fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Age' reads as the spiritual movement, but 'New' is an anagram signal and 'accepts' a container signal. Londoners have long called their city simply 'town'.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a loose afternoon gown worn by Victorian and Edwardian women, a dress for receiving at tea.

clue.text: No alternative to this dramatic style

definitions.text: No alternative to this dramatic style

parts.words: No alternative to this dramatic style
parts.note: the Japanese theatre form is also spelt No, so 'No' is an alternative spelling of it

explanation.surface: There is nothing else but this theatrical manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No alternative' looks like 'there is no other choice', but No is just another spelling of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is classical Japanese masked drama, a dramatic style also spelt No.

clue.text: Finished and got excited

definitions.meaning: brought to a close, as a meeting

explanation.surface: Done, and thrilled about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A business can be closed down and a person agitated, both expressed by the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Opening of tomb in sacred surroundings disputed thus?

indicators.note: in says the opening letter is placed within the sacred word

parts.note: holy means sacred, here forming the surroundings

indicators.note: opening of asks for the first letter of the word tomb

explanation.surface: Breaking into a grave in a holy place was fiercely argued over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' suggests opening the tomb; it is just its first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hotly disputed is argued with passion, so the adverb shows how it was fought over.

clue.text: Historian found point dividing Churchill, say, and America

indicators.note: dividing says the point sits between the other two pieces

parts.note: Churchill is an example of a national hero
US stands for the United States of America
a dot is a point

explanation.surface: A historian finds a gap between Churchill and America.
explanation.walkthrough: Herodotus was the ancient Greek called the father of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Herodotus was the fifth-century BC Greek writer known as the father of history.
